meta.note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation 5 list as published by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this bounty opened; the two sources agree on every name, description and grade. Guides are this entry's own words, written from the official descriptions — the game was a day old when this guide was built, so where a description does not pin down a place or a step, the guide says so instead of inventing one.

sources.label: PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list (grades and PSN counts)

trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is no extra task of its own. Work the roadmap in order: finish the story, clear the stranger strands and activities, sweep the collectibles and counts, then finish the money goals and 100% completion. A Long Road (100%) is the last big gate before this pops.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Gone Fishing. Story trophies unlock by playing the story, so this one cannot be missed — keep following the main missions and it pops when the mission ends. Fishing itself is also an activity: beating Cal in a fishing challenge is a separate trophy (Baited My Tackle).
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. Chapter trophies are unmissable: play the main missions in order and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. Use the chapter as a natural checkpoint — before moving on, it is a good moment to try the activities that chapter's area opens up.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable and pops when the chapter closes. Chapter 2 is where the money side of the game opens up — the laundering behind Dime on the Dollar and the spending behind Treat Yo Self start to become possible, so keep an eye on Marked Bills from here on.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. Unmissable — it pops at the chapter's end. By now the map is well opened up, so this is a good point to start the long counts in the background: discovering vehicles for Whip It Good and exploring for The Goodtime State happen naturally as you travel between missions.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. Unmissable — it pops at the chapter's end. After Chapter 4 the story is in its final stretch, so finish any partner-dependent trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) while a partner is still around for missions, and start the stranger strands if you have not yet.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. This is the story's gold trophy and it is unmissable — it pops when the credits roll. After the finale the game continues in free roam, so anything not yet done (collectibles, counts, money goals, 100% completion) can still be finished afterwards.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies are unmissable — play the mission to its end and the trophy pops. If a mission ever feels hard, the game lets you retry it; there is no penalty for failing and trying again.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are story missions, so this trophy is unmissable — complete the heist and it pops. Heists are also good practice for the robbery trophies later (Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play), which use the same escape-the-heat skills in free roam.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. Unmissable — it pops when the mission ends. Story mission trophies never require a special approach: finishing the mission is the whole requirement, on any difficulty.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. Unmissable — it pops when the mission ends. The mission's name is also a hint about the game's music scene; the trophy itself only asks that the mission be completed.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown. Unmissable — it pops when the mission ends. Note the airport: VCIA is also the setting of Catch Me If You Can, so while you are there for this mission, remember that the unscheduled-departure trophy is a separate, timing-sensitive one to attempt around the airport.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Unmissable — it pops when the mission ends. Despite the wintry name, the requirement is only the mission's completion; no weather or side condition is named in the official description.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion, which the game tracks in its stats or checklist screen. This is the last big gate before the platinum and it folds in the story, the stranger strands, the activities and the collectibles — essentially everything the other trophies ask for, plus the game's own completion checklist. Save it for last: clear the roadmap's stages 1 to 3 first, then use the in-game completion tracker to find whatever is still missing.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts across Leonida — jumps, ramps and stunt spots the game counts as you land them. The count is cumulative and carries across the whole game, so chip away at it whenever you pass a ramp or a jump in free roam rather than grinding it in one sitting. Fast vehicles and the map's many ramps make this a background task that finishes itself over a full playthrough.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity in the game at least once — racing, fishing, the shooting range, arcade games, bowling, drone races, meditation, hunting and the rest. You do not need to win or finish any of them, just sample each one. Open the activities list in-game and tick them off one by one; the ones you have not tried yet are the ones left to sample.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 challenges in total, as PSNProfiles lists the count PlayStation tracks. Visit a shooting range and work through its challenge list; each challenge shows its gold-medal target, so you can see exactly what score or time to beat. Use the range's own weapons, take it one challenge at a time, and retry any challenge freely — failed attempts cost nothing but time.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations around Leonida. Drone races are won by flying the course faster than the rival drones, so learn each course's line before pushing for the win — a practice run that maps the turns is worth more than a rushed first attempt. The trophy pops when every location has a win.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — each race only counts once, so you need 20 distinct events, not 20 wins on the same track. Work through the race list across Leonida, trying a new event each time, and pick vehicle classes you are comfortable with. Races you have already won do not count again, so keep moving to new ones.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are the game's fishing activity — cast, hook and land the better catch against Cal's result. If you lose, challenge him again; the trophy only needs one win. The fishing in Gone Fishing is the story's introduction to it, so you will already know the basics by the time you meet Cal.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish a full game at any arcade machine in Leonida, from start to its end screen. Any arcade game counts, so pick the one you enjoy most or find easiest. Arcades are also worth visiting for Master of None, which asks you to try each activity type once.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand by completing his final mission. Stranger missions appear as you explore Leonida — follow Andy's strand through its missions until its finale. Stranger finals are story-like and unmissable once you start the strand; the only requirement is to see it through to the end.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand by completing his final mission. Kenton's strand involves boats — the trophy's name is a nod to that — so expect his missions to take you out on the water. See the strand through to its finale and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand by completing his final mission. Billy's strand is the lone-rider one, so expect his missions to be solo rides. Follow the strand to its finale and the trophy pops when the last mission ends.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the game's Strangers & Freaks-style side characters, including Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, whose final missions each have their own trophy. Stranger strands appear as you explore, marked in the world; each strand is a short chain of missions ending in a finale. Finish any 8 strands and this silver pops. Track your progress in the checklist — the five named stranger finals are the natural first five.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand by completing his final mission. Randy's strand is the supply-and-demand one, so expect his missions to revolve around moving goods. See the strand through to its finale and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand by completing his final mission. Follow Tyrone's strand through its missions until the finale — the trophy pops when the last mission ends. Tyrone is one of the five named stranger finals, so his strand also counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet places in the world where your character can sit and meditate — find each one and complete a meditation there. The trophy pops when every spot has been used. Meditation spots are spread over the whole map, so this pairs naturally with The Goodtime State (explore all of Leonida).
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a specific animal Bret asks you to track down, not just any wildlife. Bret's hunt is a stranger-style request: follow his lead to the animal, track it and take it down. The official description does not name the animal or the location, so follow Bret's directions in-game rather than a fixed spot from this guide.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set is complete when you hold every card in it. Search the world thoroughly — cards are a pure collectible hunt with no combat requirement — and use the in-game collection screen to see which sets are still missing cards. Three finished sets pop the silver.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK service at 100 different locations across Leonida. WAiNK is the game's in-world service you interact with at marked spots — visit a new spot, use it, and move on; each location counts once. The count is cumulative, so fold it into your exploration: every time you reach a new area for The Goodtime State, look for a WAiNK spot there too.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's challenge list, which covers stunts, races, activities and more. Challenges are the small goals the game tracks as you play, so many will complete themselves during a full playthrough; check the challenge list in-game to see which kinds you have left and pick the easiest remaining ones to reach 50.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. This one needs your partner present, so attempt it during a mission or free-roam stretch when a partner is with you — do not leave it until after the story, when partners may no longer be around. Once the wanted level is at 4 stars, break line of sight, hide until the stars clear, and the trophy pops on escaping. Flagged as partner-dependent in this guide's missables list.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you — attempt while a partner is available in the story.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, rob three shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level — the robberies must be back-to-back and the heat must stay on the whole time. Like Hot Together this needs a partner present, so do it while a partner is available. Plan a route past three shops, keep moving between them, and do not let the wanted level drop to zero before the third robbery. Flagged as partner-dependent in this guide's missables list.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you, and three robberies in a row — attempt while a partner is available.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive or ride each one and the game logs it as discovered. The count is cumulative across the whole game and includes the everyday traffic of Leonida, so variety is the key: try a new vehicle whenever you see one you have not driven. Check the in-game vehicle log to see how many you have found. This finishes naturally over a full playthrough with a habit of swapping rides.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-down aiming mode. Find a fight with at least five enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and drop five of them before the effect ends. A busy shootout with grouped enemies is the place to try it; if you only get four, retry the fight — failed attempts cost nothing.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — leave the airport in a way the schedule did not plan. The official description ties this trophy to VCIA itself, so attempt it when the story takes you to the airport (Hi-Jacked and the VCIA Takedown mission are the natural moments). The exact trigger is not pinned down in the description, so try the obvious: grab a plane at the airport and take off without following a mission's script. Flagged as timing-sensitive in this guide's missables list.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to VCIA — attempt it when the story takes you to the airport.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke, not a set of instructions — it names the Rhino, the game's tank. The trophy is about the Rhino: get into one and use it. Rhinos appear at military sites and in wanted-level chaos, so take one for a drive and cause some mayhem; the trophy pops from using the tank as the description implies. The exact trigger is not pinned down in the official description, so this guide does not invent a step count for it.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — get in, take the goods and get out before anyone spots you. Go quiet: avoid cameras and guards, move when the store is calm, and leave before the alarm goes up. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again later — the store can be robbed again.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Bank vaults are the big robberies of free roam: break in, take the vault's contents and get away clean. Each vault counts once, so you need five different vaults. Plan an escape route before you go in — a fast car parked close by — and do not linger after the alarm. Five successful vault robberies pop the silver.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida — find one, stop it, take its cash and get away before the cops close in. A roadblock or a well-placed hit stops the truck; then grab the money and drive. One clean truck robbery pops the trophy.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore every region of Leonida — the whole map, from Vice City to the far corners of the state. The game tracks which areas you have visited, so travel everywhere: drive the highways, visit each town and district, and check the map for blank spots. This pairs naturally with the collectible hunts (WAiNK spots, meditation spots, cards), which are also spread across the map.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida — one per gang. Gangs run their own off-the-books operations around the state; find each gang's operation, hit it and get away. The trophy pops when every gang has been robbed once. Keep a note of which gangs you have done, since the description asks for each gang, not just any of them.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — go to a bar or spot on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail and take in the view. This is a quiet moment trophy, not a challenge: head to Ocean Beach, find somewhere serving drinks with a sea view, and the trophy pops when the moment plays out.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom's glass and out the other side. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or line one up at the entrance, and floor it through the front. The trophy pops on the dramatic exit; the showroom's cars are replaceable, so do not worry about the damage.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — bowl a game there. Head to the bowling alley, play a full game and follow through on your throws. Any game counts; the trophy is about showing up and playing at this specific alley, which is also where the Ten Pin trophy's melee drive-by happens.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The description is vague — a partnership with mass appeal — and it does not name the activity, the partner or the place. The likeliest reading from the description is a partner-related goal tied to how widely your duo is known, but this guide will not invent a specific step the official description does not give. Check the in-game activities and partner options, and watch for a partnership goal that mentions appeal or fame; this guide's sources are the official list, and the trigger is not yet pinned down.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: The description is a single line about choices, and it does not say which choice or when. The honest reading is that a story decision you make triggers this trophy — and a choice, once made, may not be undoable. So keep a manual save before major story decisions, especially in the final chapters, so you can revisit a choice if you need to. Flagged as choice-based in this guide's missables list, because a decision locked in by the story is the one kind of trophy a replay would be needed to fix.
trophies.missableNote: A story choice may lock it in — keep a manual save before major decisions.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: The description is a riddle — second time's the charm — and it does not name what you retry. The likeliest reading is a task that pops when you succeed on a second attempt after failing once, whether a mission, a challenge or an activity. Do not force it: play normally, and if something fails once and you clear it on the retry, this is the trophy that may pop. This guide does not invent a specific task the official description does not give.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: The description is a reaction, not an instruction — something strange happens and the trophy pops. The likeliest reading is a secret encounter or easter egg somewhere in Leonida, the kind of odd event players stumble on while exploring. The official description does not name the place or the event, so this guide will not invent one: explore the stranger corners of the map, follow odd sights, and check the guide sources as players map the trigger.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl people over with a melee drive-by — attack from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon and knock down your targets like bowling pins. Drive slowly past a group on foot, swing the melee weapon from the vehicle and bowl them over. The bowling alley from Let's Go Bowling is the thematic home of this one, but any group on foot works for the drive-by itself.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from heists and robberies — dirty money you cannot spend directly — and your contacts clean it for a cut. Keep feeding bills to your contacts through the story and the free-roam robberies; the $250,000 is cumulative earnings from laundering, not a single haul. This is a late-game money goal, so fold it into the roadmap's final stage with Treat Yo Self.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in Leonida — clothes, weapons, food, vehicle mods, anything the shops sell. The total is cumulative across every shop, so it finishes naturally if you buy gear, upgrade cars and eat out through the game. If you reach the endgame short of the total, the fastest top-up is vehicle modifications and high-end clothing, which are the priciest single purchases.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase every garage property in Leonida. Garages are the properties that store your vehicles — buy each one the game offers, across the map. They cost money, so this is a late-game purchase once the story and robberies have filled your wallet; it pairs with the money goals in the roadmap's final stage. The trophy pops when the last garage is bought.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles around Leonida, bring them to the app's registration and log each one — ten different vehicles in total. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles): every new vehicle you find is a candidate to register, so register as you discover rather than hunting ten at the end.
trophies.name: On the Spot
